brief.subject: PTINs expire Dec. 31, plus new IRS reporting rule fixes
brief.headline: Tax preparers must renew PTINs before Dec. 31; IRS updates two proposed rules
brief.dek: PTIN renewal season opens, opportunity zone reporting rules get corrections, and voters split on state taxes on the wealthy.
brief.lede: Current preparer tax identification numbers expire on Dec. 31, 2026. Anyone paid to prepare returns needs a renewed PTIN to keep filing in the new year.

sections.heading: PTIN renewal season is here
bullets: Current PTINs expire Dec. 31, 2026, so preparers face a year-end deadline.
Paid return preparers must hold a valid PTIN, and it must be renewed every year.
Bookkeepers who prepare client returns need a current number before the 2027 filing season.

sections.heading: IRS tweaks two proposed rules
bullets: The IRS corrected proposed opportunity zone reporting regulations (REG-116506-25), first published Sept. 11, 2026.
Those rules would require qualified opportunity funds to file information returns and send statements to investors who sell their stakes.
Qualified opportunity zone businesses would also have to send statements to the funds holding interests in them.
The Dec. 15, 2026 hearing on the scholarship tax credit rules (REG-117199-25) is now telephone-only, at 10 a.m. ET.

sections.heading: Voters split on taxing the wealthy
bullets: About 52.9% of California voters rejected a one-time 5% wealth tax in preliminary results, versus 47.1% in favor.
Washington voters upheld a 9.9% tax on household incomes above $1 million.
The Washington tax still faces a major court challenge that could reshape the state's budget and tax policy.

sections.heading: Fake IRS agent pleads guilty
bullets: Sandra Vega, 48, of Pecos, NM, pleaded guilty to four counts of wire fraud.
She also admitted to impersonating a federal officer and demanding something of value.
The case shows IRS impersonation schemes remain a live risk for business owners and their clients.

items.snippet: Tax professionals who prepare tax returns must have a valid preparer tax identification number, which must be renewed each year. Current PTINs expire on Dec. 31, 2026.

items.title: Voters Upheld Washington ‘Millionaires Tax.’ Will Courts Do the Same?
items.snippet: The 9.9% tax on household incomes above $1 million still faces a high-profile legal battle with major implications for the state’s budget and tax policy.

items.title: Billionaire Tax Rejected by California Voters
items.snippet: Preliminary results as of Monday evening showed about 52.9% of voters rejected the one-time, 5% wealth tax, compared to 47.1% who voted for it.

items.title: Notice: [Proposed Extension of Information Collection Request Submitted for Public Comment; Comment Request on Burden Related to the Qualified Intermediary (QI), Withholding Foreign Partnership (WP), and Withholding Foreign Trust (WT) Application and Account Management System
items.snippet: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, the IRS is inviting comments on the information collection request outlined in this notice.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts; Hearing
items.snippet: This document provides a notice of proposed rulemaking (CC- 00349938-26) published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. The proposed regulations provided guidance regarding eligible investments, which are the only assets in which the Trump account may be invested before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains 18.
